issues.description: Insecure ID generation using Math.random(). Predictable IDs can be exploited for enumeration attacks or IDOR vulnerabilities.
issues.suggestion: Use crypto.randomUUID() instead: `import { randomUUID } from 'crypto'; function generateId(): string { return randomUUID(); }`

issues.description: Manual HTML entity encoding for XSS prevention is fragile and may miss edge cases. This approach doesn't handle all contexts (URL, JavaScript, CSS).
issues.suggestion: Use a well-tested library like DOMPurify or the platform's built-in sanitization (e.g., textContent in browsers). If manual encoding is required, document the specific context (HTML text content only) and add comprehensive test coverage.

issues.description: Email regex validation is overly simplistic and may allow invalid emails or reject valid ones (e.g., doesn't handle internationalized domains, quoted strings, or RFC 5322 edge cases).
issues.suggestion: Consider using a robust email validation library like 'validator.js' or 'email-validator', or rely on the email provider's validation after sending a confirmation email. Document that this is basic format checking only.

issues.description: Input validation only checks for falsy values, which means empty strings pass validation. This may allow creation of users with empty names/emails.
issues.suggestion: Add explicit length and whitespace checks: `if (!input.email?.trim() || !input.name?.trim()) { throw new Error('Email and name are required and cannot be empty'); }`

codeQuality.summary: Overall clean and well-structured code with good security practices (parameterized queries, input validation, XSS protection). Primary concern is insecure ID generation using Math.random() which should use crypto.randomUUID() for production systems.

Email validation logic used by createUser; regex correctness is critical for security and data integrity. No tests verify it accepts valid emails or rejects invalid ones.
XSS protection function; must correctly escape HTML special characters. No tests verify it escapes all dangerous characters or handles edge cases.
Should handle empty strings gracefully without errors.

testCoverage.summary: This new fixture file has zero test coverage. The riskiest gaps are createUser (critical validation and database persistence logic), isValidEmail (email validation regex), and sanitizeInput (XSS protection).

suggestions.description: Make User interface properties readonly to prevent accidental mutations after creation.
suggestions.benefits: Prevents accidental property mutations, makes immutability explicit, and catches bugs at compile time.

suggestions.description: Make CreateUserInput properties readonly since input DTOs should be immutable.
suggestions.benefits: Prevents mutation of input data, enforces immutability at the API boundary.

suggestions.description: Use a lookup table with Object.entries to reduce repetitive replace calls.
suggestions.benefits: Single regex pass instead of four; easier to add new entities; clearer mapping of character to entity.

suggestions.description: Extract validation logic into a separate validator function to improve testability and separation of concerns.
suggestions.benefits: Validation logic is independently testable; createUser is more focused on orchestration; easier to reuse validation elsewhere.

suggestions.description: Use optional chaining and nullish coalescing for more concise truthy checks, or be explicit about empty string validation.
suggestions.benefits: Catches edge case of whitespace-only strings; more explicit validation of meaningful input.

refactorings.summary: Overall clean and well-structured code with good separation of concerns. Main opportunities are adding readonly modifiers for immutability, extracting validation logic into a testable function, and minor optimizations to the sanitization approach.

recommendations.description: Add comprehensive test coverage for the createUser function which handles critical user creation, validation, and database persistence logic. Currently has 0% test coverage.
Replace Math.random() with crypto.randomUUID() for secure, unpredictable ID generation to prevent enumeration attacks and IDOR vulnerabilities.
Add test coverage for security-critical functions isValidEmail and sanitizeInput to verify they correctly validate emails and escape XSS attack vectors.
Add tests for all validation branches in createUser: missing email, missing name, and invalid email format error paths.
Extract validation logic from createUser into a separate validateUserInput function to improve testability and separation of concerns.
Enhance input validation to explicitly reject empty strings and whitespace-only inputs using trim() checks to prevent creation of users with invalid data.
Consider replacing manual HTML entity encoding with a well-tested library like DOMPurify, or document that sanitizeInput only handles HTML text content context.
Add readonly modifiers to User and CreateUserInput interface properties to enforce immutability and prevent accidental mutations.
